title: Project render for out-of-tree unmanaged worktrees fails closed instead of aliasing to base repo_id
wanted_capability: Decide-me carried out of closed gap-8c25a414: an arbitrary out-of-tree user worktree (git worktree add ../sibling) resolves Read to the base project but Write to None, so project render falls to raw-path passthrough with zero entries and the destructive-shrink guard refuses the write. This fail-closed behavior is deliberate (documented in the resolver) and safe, but it means renders in such worktrees silently do nothing useful. Wanted: a decision whether render should use the Read-gate scope for entry filtering while writing into the checkout (making out-of-tree worktrees first-class), or whether fail-closed stays and gets a clearer operator-facing message explaining why the render was refused.
missing_primitive: write-scope aliasing (or explicit refusal messaging) for out-of-tree unmanaged worktrees in project render
fallback_used: Run renders from the base checkout or a managed worktree; the shrink guard prevents damage meanwhile.
resolution_note: obsolete: project render no longer falls through to a raw-path passthrough with zero entries. Since 23b83104 (checkout authority phase zero), bbox_render resolves identity before opening any target (src/tools/render.rs): in bridge mode resolve_project_write (src/tools/scope.rs) rejects an out-of-tree unmanaged worktree (Write finds no managed alias; the Read fallback accepts only base-rooted resolutions, and resolve_scope_and_checkout_dir returns the worktree root), so render bails with error.attachment_required before writing; catalog mode fails with error.project_selector_unknown via validate_project_selection. The fail-closed path is now an explicit refusal, not a silent empty render caught by the shrink guard. Making out-of-tree worktrees first-class render targets would be a new feature request.
